title: Embedding memoization index with tenant-window probes
creator: Priya Raman
description:
Problem: Reranking endpoints spend a large fraction of their tail latency and cost recomputing embeddings for requests that contain repeated content or small variations (e.g., identical prefixes, copy-paste snippets). Current prefix/prefix-fingerprint caches reduce some work but suffer from noisy invalidation and tenant cross-talk. This ticket proposes a tenant-aware 'memoization index' for embeddings plus an active staleness probing layer (tenant-window probes) to keep TTLs tight without risking stale reranking signals.

Goals: Deploy a low-latency, shardable memoization layer that: 1) deduplicates identical/near-identical embedding inputs within and across tenants; 2) supports fast negative lookups (cheap false-negative fallback to compute) to avoid blocking; 3) provides tight TTLs using lightweight probes to detect content churn per-tenant; 4) exposes metrics and knobs to trade latency vs. freshness.

High-level design:
- Input normalization: apply deterministic Unicode normalization, strip punctuation according to config, and canonicalize whitespace before hashing.
- Content signature: use a salted SipHash-2-4 fingerprint combined with a short simhash (64-bit) for cheap near-duplicate detection. Salt is tenant-scoped to avoid cross-tenant collisions and to support tenant-level invalidation.
- Memoization index: an in-memory LRU/LFU hybrid per-shard map keyed by the content signature; values store embedding pointer (or compact 16-byte selector), last-seen timestamp, and generation id. Store compacted embeddings in a shared blob store when size > threshold.
- Tenant-window probes: for each tenant we maintain a lightweight probe queue that periodically samples a small representative set of keys and re-computes embeddings to detect drift. Probe frequency and sample size are configurable per-tenant and tied to observed edit rates. When drift exceeds threshold, the system triggers targeted invalidation and optionally increases probe aggressiveness.
- Invalidation signals: explicit model-upgrade hooks, tenant webhook (external content edits), automatic probe-triggered churn, and TTL expiry. Invalidation is soft (generation bump) to permit in-flight reads to continue but forces recompute on next miss.
- Sharding & consistency: index is shard-local (consistent hashing by tenant shard). A lightweight gossip for generation ids across replicas ensures fast propagation of invalidations without heavy cross-shard locking.
- Fall back: on a negative or stale memoization result, fall back to full embedding computation and write-through policy if result passes freshness checks.

Trade-offs considered:
- Memory vs latency: keeping expanded embeddings in-memory speeds reads but multiplies memory. Solution: compact selectors + external blob store for large entries and an adaptive in-memory hotset driven by access frequency.
- False positives for near-duplicate detection: simhash cutoff must be tuned per workload; conservative defaults chosen to prefer correctness over hit-rate.
- Probe overhead vs freshness: probes add cost; we throttle by tenant and correlate probe budget to tenant activity and revenue tier.

Why this is different from prior cache work: existing prefix caches focus on exact prefix matches and global keys; this design emphasizes tenant-scoped memoization, near-duplicate resilience, and active staleness detection to reduce TTLs while keeping correctness for reranking applications.
acceptance_criteria: Cache reduces end-to-end embedding compute rate for rerank endpoints by >= 40% for low-entropy tenants (measured on test cohort)
P95 latency for rerank requests improves by >= 10% in the staging cluster under representative load
Cache hit rates exposed per-tenant and bucketed by simhash distance; default simhash cutoff validated against training prompts
No observable rerank quality regression: mean reciprocal rank (MRR) within 0.5% of baseline on evaluation set
Probe-driven invalidation works: when we simulate tenant content churn, probes detect and reduce TTL within 3 probe cycles
Rollout plan exists: canary + 25% traffic + 100% with automatic rollback on increased error or MRR drop

comments: 2025-02-12 Priya Raman: Created ticket after spike showed 48% repeated-prefix rate for our small-tenant testset. Initial data and motivation attached in design doc.

2025-02-22 Design review notes (Maya, Hana): agree on tenant salt but requested an explicit migration plan for old keys; recommend generation-id approach and a one-week overlap window. Added migration to tasks.

2025-02-27 SRE (Anika): Concern about probe storms during incidents. We'll add circuit-breakers per-tenant and global probe budget. SRE runbook updated: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Probe+Runbook

2025-03-01 Miguel Torres: Integration tests passing on staging. Observed p95 latency improvement of 12% for rerank service under 50% traffic canary. Next: extend probe sampling to high-activity tenants and run full quality eval.
